title: Amortized 7-day rolling minimums with adaptive stream-backoff discount (probe)
creator: Anika Patel
description:
Problem: Many customers with conversational products have extremely bursty usage (e.g., chatbots with heavy day-phase traffic and idle nights) which causes sharp billing spikes and churn when minimums kick in. Single-invoice minimums (monthly/quarterly) are blunt instruments and penalize teams that are usage-bursty by design.

Proposal: Run a pricing probe that replaces a hard per-invoice minimum with an amortized 7-day rolling minimum plus an adaptive streaming discount window (stream-backoff discount). The rolling minimum smooths commit exposure for short-lived spikes while the stream-backoff discount reduces marginal per-token cost for sessions that degrade to lower sustained throughput (common in interactive agents). Together they aim to retain predictable unit economics while reducing churn for bursty customers.
hypothesis: If we apply an amortized 7-day rolling minimum (daily amortization toward a weekly floor) and a streaming backoff discount that triggers after sustained low-throughput streaming for a session, then customers with bursty daily peaks will see lower perceived variability and fewer support escalations about minimum charges, while Redwood's net revenue per active customer will remain within 5% of baseline for the cohort.
experiment_design:
Cohort selection: 200 customers with historical bursty patterns (CV of daily tokens > 2.0) randomized into control and treatment. Treatment rules: 1) Compute weekly minimum = 0.7 * current monthly micro-minimum equivalent (config param); apply amortization by charging only the max(0, weekly_minimum - sum(tokens_charged_last_7_days)) at invoice time; 2) Streaming backoff discount: for streaming sessions where average throughput drops below threshold T tokens/sec for > M seconds, apply a temporary per-output-token discount of D% for the remainder of that session and subsequent N sessions within 24h. Parameters (initial): weekly_floor_factor=0.7, T=5 tokens/sec, M=30s, D=30%, N=3.

Billing logic edge-cases: provide a grace reconciliation window of 48h for usage adjustments; apply a safety cap (max discount exposure per org per week = 25% of expected weekly spend) to control revenue leakage.

Artifacts: simulation harness (GitHub): https://github.com/redwood-inference/pricing-experiments/tree/pm/rolling-minimums; design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PM/pages/rolling-minimums-probe
success_metrics: Primary: churn rate delta (treatment vs control) over 90 days; Secondary: net revenue per active customer change (target within ±5%), number of billing disputes/tickets related to minimums, avg daily variance (stddev) of billed amounts per org reduced by >=20% for cohort. Operational: number of incidents caused by billing logic, discount exposure as % of weekly revenue (should stay <2% during pilot).
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (2 weeks): sim-only using historical telemetry to tune T/M/D/N and weekly_floor_factor. Phase 1 (6 weeks): small pilot (20 customers) with manual monitoring and customer outreach. Phase 2 (8 weeks): expanded cohort (200 customers randomized) with automated billing pipeline and safety caps. Phase 3: analysis and decision to roll to broader cohort or iterate. Communication: preflight emails to pilot customers, in-console banner when feature enabled, and dedicated support runbook.
notes:
Trade-offs discussed: tighter floors protect revenue but reduce the benefit for bursty customers; longer amortization windows reduce churn but increase accounting complexity. Engineering feedback recommends feature-flagged rollout with a reconciliation batch job to ensure idempotent billing updates. Legal requested sample language for SQ questions about minimums — PM to provide by 2025-11-15.

Open questions: Should streaming backoff be measured per session or per token-substream (function calls)? How to expose amortized weekly floor in the Console pricing preview UI?

Recent updates: 2025-11-07 - ran sim for 12 months of telemetry, found expected discount exposure of 1.6% at weekly_floor_factor=0.7 and D=30%; 2025-11-08 - ENG signed off on billing connector changes contingent on reconciliation job SLA.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Simulation shows <2.5% revenue leakage at production parameter set; 2) Billing pipeline implements amortized weekly floor and stream-backoff discount behind feature flag; 3) Console shows accurate preview for pilot customers; 4) Support runbook and legal SQ language approved; 5) Pilot executed without more than one P1 billing incident.
customer_outreach_plan: Targeted opt-in invites to pilot customers with bursty profiles; include a short FAQ, example invoices comparing baseline vs amortized floor for typical burst patterns, and an opt-out button. Post-pilot survey to collect qualitative feedback.
audit_trail_notes: Pilot will log every discount decision and amortization calculation to an immutable billing audit index for 180 days per compliance guidance.
escalation_path: Billing incidents -> Billing Eng on-call -> PM -> Head of Revenue -> Legal
estimated_impact: Estimated to reduce churn in bursty cohort by 12-18% and reduce billing disputes by ~40% for participating customers; expected net weekly revenue variance within ±4% for pilot parameters.
privacy_considerations: No new customer PII is required for experiment; use aggregated org-level token counters. Retention of audit logs follows existing KMS-encrypted storage policies.
implementation_notes: ENG to implement feature-flagged billing module and reconciliation batch. Add metrics hooks for discount exposure, per-org weekly amortized floor consumption, and streaming backoff triggers. Ensure idempotency and race-free invoices when users trigger refunds/adjustments during grace window.
